audit.whatIsWrong: Courage is called a 'damage-cut' and 'tenacity-W', but nothing says what the tenacity does to you — and it is the whole reason his answer beats your engage.
audit.why: Riot's Courage text: activating it gives 'a shield and tenacity for a brief moment followed by a lesser amount of damage reduction for a longer duration', on 22/19.5/17/14.5/12. Tenacity shortens crowd control, so a Courage popped as you land Shield Vault cuts the stun you paid 13 seconds for. That is not a damage problem, it is a timing problem: bait the 22s first.
audit.corrected: Courage's tenacity shortens your Shield Vault stun — bait its 22s before you commit, do not stun into it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The coverage packet records that no Garen ability is named anywhere in the content layer, and Decisive Strike is described only as 'his Q silence'.
audit.why: Riot's Decisive Strike text: he 'gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him', and the next attack silences. The slow-break matters directly — Grand Starfall lands with a slow, and Decisive Strike removes it on an 8s cooldown, so the ultimate does not hold him for the follow-up. Judgment is the 9s spin, Perseverance the out-of-combat regen, Demacian Justice the 120s true-damage execute.
audit.corrected: All five named; Decisive Strike stated as an 8s slow-break plus silence, which is what beats a Grand Starfall follow-up.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appears anywhere, and Demacian Justice is described as a 'missing-HP true-damage execute'.
audit.why: Courage 22s at rank 1, Decisive Strike 8s, Judgment 9s, Demacian Justice 120s. The true damage is real and is why armour does nothing about the execute — _missing-interactions.json flags exactly that. The missing-health scaling is not in Riot's text for this ability, so I dropped that half rather than assert it.
audit.corrected: Real numbers added; the execute described as true damage that ignores resistances, without the unverified missing-HP clause.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are yours: your point-and-click W stun plus empowered Q out-trades anything Garen has before his passive regen comes online, so force the all-in early. The catch is his W — if he pops it your burst gets cut, and his Q silences whatever you try to follow up with, so bait the W down before you commit your stun. Don't poke into a Garen who's about to back off into a bush; his regen heals your chip damage the second you stop.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are yours: Shield Vault's leap-stun plus empowered Comet Spear out-trades anything Garen has before Courage is ranked, so force the all-in early. The catch is Courage itself — popped as you land the stun, its tenacity shortens the stun you spent 13 seconds on, and Decisive Strike silences the follow-up. Bait its 22 seconds first. Don't chip a Garen who can walk off; Perseverance regenerates it all back.

edits.before: Level 3 onward this evens out — your E-block can eat his Q-silence strike and your empowered-Q poke still chips, but his W damage-cut neuters your all-in burst whenever it's up. At 6 his R is the lane-changer: it's a missing-HP true-damage execute, so the all-ins you'd win on a healthbar suddenly kill YOU under the threshold. Don't dive a low Garen — instead use your own R to roam and cash your early tempo into kills elsewhere.
edits.after: Level 3 onward this evens out — facing him lets Aegis Assault eat the Decisive Strike hit and empowered-Q still chips, but Courage's 22s cuts both your burst and your stun whenever it is up. At 6 Demacian Justice is a 120s true-damage execute, so the all-in you would win on a health bar kills YOU under the threshold. Note too that Decisive Strike breaks slows on 8s, so Grand Starfall's slow will not hold him.

edits.before: At level 1 your point-and-click W stun damage is one of the best in the game — all-in before his passive regen matters.
edits.after: At level 1 Shield Vault's leap-stun damage is one of the best in the game — all-in now, while Courage does not exist.

edits.after: A coinflip now — Courage's tenacity shortens your stun and Decisive Strike silences the follow-up, so it comes down to baiting the 22s.

notes: Two mechanics were doing the work in this lane and neither was on the page. Courage grants tenacity, not just damage reduction, so popping it as you land Shield Vault shortens the stun — the counterplay is baiting its 22 seconds rather than out-damaging it. And Decisive Strike 'breaks free of all slows' on an 8s cooldown, which specifically defeats Grand Starfall's landing slow; nothing warned you about spending a 180s ultimate on a champion who removes its only lasting effect. I also removed the 'missing-HP' half of the Demacian Justice description: Riot's text for it is one line about attempting to execute, and only the true damage is confirmed by the kit flags.
